title: Pony experiences, home-ed club and creative arts near Bath
description: Creative Rein brings together ponies, outdoor learning and creative arts for children in Bathford, five minutes from Bath. Home-Ed Club, alternative provision, toddler sessions, events and pony parties.

sections.heading: Ponies, fresh air and making things, on a hill above Bath.
sections.lede: Small groups and 1-to-1 sessions for children aged 5 to 18, with toddler mornings for the little ones. No horse experience needed.

sections.heading: Equine Learning. Outdoor Education. Creative Arts.
sections.body:
Creative Rein is a home education and alternative learning environment in Bath, offering riding, outdoor learning and creative art.

We bring together horses, outdoor exploration and creative practice in a setting where everyone can discover and pursue different interests and ways of learning.

We welcome enquiries from home-educating families, and from those seeking additional opportunities for children who benefit from smaller, supportive settings.

sections.heading: Home Education
sections.body:
Creative Rein offers term-time learning to enrich your child's journey in life. Our weekly Home-Ed Club combines creative arts, equine activities and outdoor learning. It's a place to develop, build experience and socialise.

Each session has its own theme, with activities adapted to suit different ages and interests. Our small-group approach allows for a more personal experience, with time to explore individual interests as well as enjoying the social side of being part of an engaging group.

No previous horse experience is needed and riding is entirely optional. It's simply about being you.

image.alt: The wooden art room, with a long table, chairs and paintings pegged along the wall

sections.heading: Alternative Provision
sections.tagline: A different way to learn, a different place to belong
sections.body:
Not every child thrives in a traditional classroom. Some need a different environment, a different pace, or simply the opportunity to discover what they are capable of outside a school setting.

Our approach is centred around practical, meaningful activities and opportunities to develop confidence, independence, communication and social connections.

Although some children may enjoy being part of a small group, others may initially feel more comfortable with individual engagement. That's why we offer 1-to-1 sessions, where a child can take part without pressure.

EOTAS and EHCP funding where applicable.

image.alt: Two people leading a brown and white pony down a tree-lined lane

sections.heading: Little Rein Club
sections.body:
We want your child to feel safe and confident around horses: comfortable touching them, interacting with them, or simply being in their presence.

Our gentle early years sessions bring together pony time, outdoor adventures, crafts and learning through play.
